the components, Storybook for the scheme with mode and brand toggles and usage rules

scheme.json, AGENTS.md, the skill, llms.txt, CI and a README

pnpm test:create: pack, create, npm install, build tokens, Storybook and docs

items.title: Components scope: each scheme picks its inventory from the shadcn catalogue
in: grammar components scope with the five method questions and a missing-component situation
grammar catalogue: the shadcn/ui new-york-v4 UI components with families
every scheme answers the components questions and lists its inventory, in and notable out, each with why
inventory shown as N of M in the docs, open-ds show and AGENTS.md, with built or not yet built

items.title: Token linkage, values only on primitives, and a subtle living style guide
in: semantic and component tokens shown as links to the primitive they end at, light and dark
primitives listed per foundation with raw values and a live sample
a specimen per foundation drawn from the scheme's CSS variables (type set in the scheme's scenario text)
shadows moved to primitives so no semantic token holds a raw value
site scope pages show links instead of raw values on decisions

items.title: Each scheme shows its UI with its own content, data, status meanings and voice
in: samples in every scheme: screen, actions, statuses with meaning and why, table, figures, field, messages, confirm, card, tabs, menu
danger only where something failed or will be lost
Storybook stories and the site preview read the active scheme's samples; every component renders in every scheme, and its docs page says when the scheme leaves it out (OD-192)
no shared fixtures between schemes

items.title: Storybook: the canvas shows the component, one MDX docs template explains it, every component's stories built the same way
in: one MDX docs page template for every component: what it is, in or out of the inventory and why, examples, playground and controls, when to use it, component keys as links
stories files: parameters.openDs, Playground, Examples; no usage text in the canvas
the docs page follows the scheme chosen in the toolbar
created projects get the same template

items.title: Patterns in the catalogue; a data table for Dense data
in: grammar catalogue.patterns: larger parts built from catalogue items, outside the component count
schemes may carry patterns with why; every part must be in the inventory
data-table pattern on TanStack Table (shadcn Data Table guide): search, faceted filters, sorting, column choice, selection with bulk actions, pagination, density
Dense data carries it, with 24 sample alerts; stories, docs and the site list it; installs bring TanStack Table only where carried

items.title: Component reference layer: general guidance per component and variant, and each scheme's decisions, in the package and MCP
in: grammar catalogue items carry a reference: overview, apply_when, not_when, vs, variants by axis, situations, accessibility, keyboard, source (Open UX where it matches)
each scheme decides every variant of every component it carries: use, or not_used with why, with because
usage rules name the components and variants they use as data (uses)
variant axes match the built components; the CLI context and component commands and the MCP return both layers

items.title: Storybook guide: an introduction, foundations pages and one component docs template with when to use it and variants, in both Storybooks
in: an Introduction page and Foundations pages (color, typography, spacing, shape, motion) read the active scheme's tokens and answers
every component docs page shows when to use it, each variant with this scheme's decision, how the scheme uses it, words and accessibility
the repo Storybook and a created project's Storybook share the same guide
every story and docs page renders in a browser, not only builds

items.title: Every component renders in every scheme, and its docs page says when the scheme leaves it out
in: a component a scheme does not carry still renders in the repo Storybook, styled by that scheme's tokens
every scheme has its own sample content for every part a story reads; no content is shared between schemes
the docs page says clearly when the scheme leaves the component out, and why
the story canvas is white in light mode and the scheme's own canvas in dark mode
created projects still carry only the components their scheme carries

items.title: Docs: component pages from the component reference, with the Storybook embed, and a Primitives page in the docs and Storybook
in: each component page reads the same engine as the CLI and MCP (componentGuide)
each component page embeds its Storybook examples and links to Storybook

each component page shows when to use it, variants with this scheme's decisions and the answers behind them, how the scheme uses it, why, what moves, words, accessibility and keyboard, code and component keys
a Primitives section of its own, next to Foundations, in the docs and in Storybook: every primitive by kind, with a sample of its value and what points to it (OD-195)

items.title: Docs: branded and visual, wearing the design system
in: the top bar carries the design system's name, version and sections, with Built with Open DS on the right
the home shows a product screen from the system's own components and samples, the answers it cites most, and tiles into every section
the colour page shows the key colours, the surfaces in light and dark, and each status in use with its contrast
component pages show the live story, each variant live with its decision and answers, the rules as do and don't, and the answers as cards
primitive colours show as ramps; the same visual styles ship in a created project's docs

items.title: Docs component pages: each variant a full-width section, and each answer a contained card in three steps
in: each variant has its own section: a live sample, what it is for (with use when and not when), this scheme's decision, and the answers behind it
each answer is one card: the answer, what it decided for the component and what else it shapes, and what would move if it changed
the steps stack inside the same card on a phone

items.title: Skills use the component reference and follow the Orchestra skill standard
in: front matter: name, a description with what and Use when in at most 25 words, and the tools the skill uses
every skill has Why, When, Input, Run and Done, with short plain sentences
every listed tool exists and a Run step uses it; every tool, command and skill a skill names exists
review checks variants against the scheme's decisions; change lists what an answer would reopen

items.title: Tools for the skills: check_ui, check_copy, plan_change, find_token, fit_scheme
in: each tool is one engine, served as an MCP tool and a CLI command (check, copy, change, token, fit)
check_ui finds raw values, components the scheme does not carry and variants it does not use; a created project comes back clean
plan_change changes nothing: it lists what an answer reopens, or the contrast a new colour keeps in every theme
the skills use the tools: review and build run check_ui, write check_copy, change plan_change, build find_token, choose fit_scheme

items.title: MCP server instructions name only real tools and prompts, and every tool reaches agents
in: every tool and prompt the server instructions name exists
every tool is named in the instructions or in a skill's tools list
the local stdio server and the hosted server send the same instructions

items.title: Context booklets and a router in created projects, from the context engine
in: a created project has context/: one Markdown booklet per component, colour and task, a router (index.json) and a README
AGENTS.md in a project holds the read-once text and the core rules, within 4 KB
get_context and open-ds context return the short form by default, with named sections, pages for long sections, and the full answer on request
get_context file=<path> and open-ds context --file return the booklets the router lists
open-ds check reports a context/ that no longer matches the scheme; open-ds context --write regenerates it
every check_ui finding names the booklet section that answers it
the read-once text is in the MCP instructions, AGENTS.md and context/README.md
budgets, routes, fixtures and the before and after benchmark are checked with no model
